findings.title: Skill Focus / Master Craftsman skill-name slugging produces ids with literal punctuation for any Craft/Profession subtype target
findings.evidence: Lines 51449 and 51466 both build a fact's explanation id with `fact.skill_name.to_lowercase().replace(' ', "_")`. `master_craftsman_facts_from_choices`'s own test fixtures (src/rules_core/feat_effects.rs:4436-4506) use skill names like "Craft (armor)" and "Profession (siege engineer)" -- exactly the subtype-in-parens shape every real Craft/Profession skill has. Running that idiom on "Craft (armor)" yields `craft_(armor)`: lowercased, the space before `(` becomes `_`, but `(` and `)` are untouched, so the id `feat.master_craftsman_bonus.craft_(armor)` (and analogously `feat.skill_focus_bonus.craft_(alchemy)` for a Craft/Profession Skill Focus target) carries literal parentheses. This is the identical defect class `slugify_id_segment` (lines 51369-51386, added and doc-corrected 2026-08-01) exists specifically to close ("putting punctuation into an id other code matches on"), and that helper is already called three lines below at 51420 for ARG skill facts -- but not for these two call sites, whose doc comment claims the naive idiom is "fine for the plain skill names they carry", which does not hold for Craft/Profession subtypes.
findings.fix_description: Route the skill_focus and master_craftsman id-building through `slugify_id_segment(&fact.skill_name)` instead of `.to_lowercase().replace(' ', "_")`, the same way the ARG block a few lines above already does.
findings.risk_notes: Changing these ids is a behavior/wire-format change to explanation ids other code (desktop sheet, tests) may already match on for the currently-malformed value, so it needs a coordinated fix + test update, not a blind mechanical edit.

findings.title: Per-weapon attack bonus omits the PF1 size modifier that the sibling baseline attack total applies
findings.evidence: `ground_per_weapon_combat_totals` (51698-51903) computes `attack_total = base_attack_bonus + attack_ability_modifier + focus_bonus + nonproficiency_penalty` (lines 51818-51819) with no size term, and its signature (51698-51703) never receives a `size` value at all. Its sibling `compute_combat_baseline`, three functions later in the same file, sums `size.armor_class_and_attack` into the analogous `melee_attack_bonus` (lines 52039-52047) under an explicit SD-27 comment: "attack rolls take PF1 Table 8-1's size modifier -- the SAME column and the same magnitude as Armor Class". `ground_per_weapon_combat_totals` is called unconditionally for every character regardless of posture (call site src/rules_core/pilot_compute/mod.rs:8863-8871, comment: "independent of the GE-06 posture gate"), so every Small race (Gnome, Halfling) or Large race gets a wrong `combat.weapon_attack_bonus.<weapon>` for every equipped weapon it grounds, off by the size modifier the file itself fixed for the one hardcoded Longsword baseline. The function's own doc comment (51657-51697) is otherwise scrupulous about naming every excluded term (ability governance, damage total scope) but never mentions size at all, unlike every other deliberate deferral in this file, which is stated explicitly.
findings.fix_description: Thread the same `size` (from `combat_size_modifiers`) into `ground_per_weapon_combat_totals` and add `size.armor_class_and_attack` to `attack_total`, updating the detail string and adding the unknown-race diagnostic path this call site currently has no access to.
findings.risk_notes: Requires adding a `diagnostics` parameter (currently absent from this function's signature) to surface the unknown-size case the same way `compute_combat_baseline` does; touches a widely-asserted-against surface (grep shows dozens of `combat.weapon_attack_bonus.*` assertions later in the file).

findings.title: compute_combat_baseline is ~550 lines of repeated class-gated conditional-bonus boilerplate that a contribution table would collapse
findings.evidence: Between the two summed totals (`melee_attack_bonus` at 52039 and `armor_class` at 52250) there are 4 and 10 respectively near-identical blocks of the shape `let x_bonus = active_x(...).map(...).unwrap_or(0);` each followed by its own if/else detail-string builder and its own paragraph of prose in the final format! call (e.g. weapon_training/inspire_courage/touch_of_good/justice_judgment for attack; rage/inspired_rage/bloodrage/brawler/mutagen/protection_judgment/natures_whispers/challenge/draconic/armor_of_the_pit for AC). The shape is uniform enough that a `Vec<(&str, i16, &str)>`-style contribution list summed via iterator, with the detail string generated generically, would remove most of this duplication -- and would have made PC8-2's kind of drift (one twin gaining a term the other doesn't) structurally harder to introduce silently.
findings.fix_description: Extract a small `CombatBonusContribution { label, value, note }` accumulator used by both `compute_combat_baseline` and `ground_per_weapon_combat_totals`, so a new conditional bonus is added once instead of per-surface.
findings.risk_notes: The current explicit prose is deliberate for player-facing explanation quality (per this file's stated design philosophy); any refactor must preserve the exact wording of every existing detail string, which is asserted against extensively elsewhere in the file.

findings.title: `.to_lowercase().replace(' ', "_")` id-slug idiom duplicated inline next to the purpose-built slugify_id_segment helper
findings.evidence: `ground_standalone_feat_skill_facts` calls `slugify_id_segment(name: &str) -> String` (defined 51369-51386) at line 51420-51421 for ARG facts, but three other blocks in the very same function (51396, 51449, 51466) still inline the older, punctuation-unsafe `fact.skill_name.to_lowercase().replace(' ', "_")` idiom the helper was written to replace. The doc comment on `slugify_id_segment` explicitly defends keeping the old idiom at the pre-existing call sites for compatibility, but two of the three (skill_focus at 51449, master_craftsman at 51466) are not actually "plain" skill names -- see PC8-1.
findings.fix_description: N/A for this lane -- listed for cross-chunk correlation; see cross_chunk for the helper signature to grep other chunks for.
findings.risk_notes: Low risk to note; any consolidation must go through the same id-compatibility analysis PC8-1 needs.

findings.title: Natural submodule-extraction seam: feat/skill/weapon/combat-baseline grounding cluster
findings.evidence: Lines 51041-52579 form one cohesive, self-contained unit -- feat-and-skill fact grounding (`ground_arg_and_pu_feat_facts`, `ground_standalone_feat_skill_facts`), weapon identity/proficiency helpers (`normalize_weapon_identity`, `equipped_weapon_stat_block`, `character_is_proficient_with`), per-weapon totals (`ground_per_weapon_combat_totals`), and the combat baseline plus its two posture-gate functions (`compute_combat_baseline`, `unmet_combat_posture_conditions`, `unmet_selected_skill_posture_conditions`) plus their two small `require_*` helpers -- with comparatively few dependencies on the rest of the 78.5k-line file (mostly `CharacterInput`, `AbilityModifiers`, `ComputationExplanation/Diagnostic`, and per-class `active_*_bonus` accessors defined elsewhere). This is a strong candidate for a `combat_baseline.rs` submodule.
findings.risk_notes: None for reporting; extraction itself would need visibility (pub(crate)) auditing across the whole file, out of scope for this lane.

findings.title: Chunk is almost entirely inline #[cfg(test)] modules from line 52594 onward
findings.evidence: A `^fn |^pub fn |^pub(crate) fn |^impl |^struct ` scan over lines 52594-70000 (via grep) finds zero top-level production items; every line in that range is inside one of ~30 sequential `#[cfg(test)] mod ..._tests { ... }` blocks (multiclass_bab_save_stacking_generalization_tests, chassis_unsupported_diagnostics_name_the_real_gate_tests, prestige_class_entry_gate_wiring_tests, untabled_base_class_chassis_wiring_tests/feature_roster_wiring_tests, save/skill-boosting-feats tests, wizard_* tests, race_ability_modifier_parity_tests, fighter_feat_choice_legality_*_tests, combat_posture_multiclass_tests, ranger/paladin/apg/acg/sorcerer/cleric/druid/barbarian/skald dispatch-widening-safety and dispatch-chassis tests). Of my assigned 51500-60500 range, only 51500-52593 (about 11%) is production code; the remaining ~89% is test code, consistent with this file's own doc comment at 52581-52593 conceding one of these modules "should" live under `tests/**` instead.
findings.risk_notes: None; informational for the overall review roll-up.
